title: Task 20j BlockNote default code block and server-first upload

bindingDecisions: Use BlockNote default codeBlock and normal slash/default insertion. Do not keep a separate ugly jixiaCodeBlock product path.
Jixia is server-first and remote-browser-first. Upload public base URLs, listen hosts, and CORS must match the browser origin.
preparation.rootProblem: Task 20i tried to make custom editor chrome more visible. The correct fix is simpler: remove the special code-block path and make the server-first upload boundary real.
doNotRepeat: Do not use Insert block as the primary code-block insertion path.
Do not add hover-only or visually foreign custom code-block controls.
Do not treat localhost-only upload URLs as valid for remote browser review.
Do not claim paste/drop success from synthetic tests alone.
preparation.firstImplementationPriority: Collapse app-level codeBlock to BlockNote type codeBlock, then make direct upload reachable from a remote browser origin before polishing secondary UX.

noSuccessWithout: slash /code creates the same authoritative BlockNote default codeBlock path used by saved app codeBlock data
custom jixiaCodeBlock and Insert block dependency are removed, disabled, or explicitly demoted from the primary UX
remote-browser upload intent, preflight/direct PUT, confirm, signed download, save, refresh, and reopen work from the recorded origin
fixture or real local API documents server-first host/public-base/CORS settings
Notebook and Project document flows are checked against the same editor path
forbiddenCompletionClaims: controls exist in source, therefore code block UX is fixed
localhost upload works, therefore server-first upload works
legacy attachment card upload works, therefore editor ingestion is unified
unit tests passed, therefore real OS paste/drop works

whatPassed: Server-first LAN fixture started and was reachable from http://10.128.253.195:5173
Manual reviewer reported image/file upload path succeeded
whatFailed: Uploaded image rendering still shows permanent function boxes/chrome above and below the image
Ready attachments are rendered as management/debug panels instead of document content
Controls are inline and always visible instead of delayed to hover, selection, right-click, or inspector surfaces
manualReview.rootCause: The upload pipeline was fixed, but the active attachment render state is wrong: ready content still uses a chrome-heavy attachment frame instead of a content-first image/file presentation.
